title: Cavity-induced intertwining of density and pairing order in a degenerate Fermi gas
authors: Sankalp Sharma, Farokh Mivehvar, Helmut Ritsch, Tomasz Wasak
abstract: Recent quantum gas cavity-QED experiments demonstrated simultaneous coupling of photons to single atom transitions as well as correlated pairs of ultracold fermions trapped inside optical cavities. This enables simultaneous control over density ordering and pairing. Using extensive numerical simulations, we show that in a transversely driven, two-component degenerate Fermi gas, the interplay of cavity-induced and bare atom--atom interactions controls not only the power threshold for self-organization, but also the type of spatial ordering in the $\mathbb Z_2$-symmetry-broken superradiant state. In the repulsive interaction regime, unpaired or weakly paired fermions first self-organize through a charge-density-wave instability, and finite-momentum pairing only occurs at much stronger pump strengths. In contrast, an attractive superfluid undergoes a joint density--pairing instability, directly entering into intertwined phase with charge-density-wave and pair-density-wave orders. At strong pumping the photon-enhanced pair interaction generates localized density and pairing order even when the bare contact interaction is repulsive. In this cavity-dominated regime strong spatial localization suppresses the long range superfluid coherence. Our results identify the role of cavity-induced atomic interactions in supporting intertwined fermionic orders and pave the way for exploring exotic states with multiple orders in highly controlled hybrid light-matter systems.
summary: This research uses numerical simulations to study how coupling a degenerate Fermi gas to an optical cavity influences the simultaneous development of density and pairing orders. The authors demonstrate that the cavity field fundamentally alters the system's ground state, leading to distinct intertwined phases depending on the nature of the atomic interactions. This work highlights the potential of cavity QED to realize and control complex, multi-ordered quantum states.
main_problem: The paper investigates the interplay and potential intertwining of density ordering and pairing order in a degenerate Fermi gas when coupled to an optical cavity.
main_result: The cavity-induced interactions can support intertwined fermionic orders, leading to distinct phase transitions depending on whether the bare interaction is repulsive or attractive.
method: The study employs extensive numerical simulations using the Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov (HFB) formalism to solve the mean-field Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a two-component degenerate Fermi gas trapped in a planar optical cavity, driven by a transverse pump laser, allowing for simultaneous control over density and pairing via cavity coupling.
key_observables: Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) instability, Pair-Density-Wave (PDW) instability, superfluid coherence, and the cavity field amplitude $|\alpha|$.
important_parameters: Bare atom-atom interaction ($g_0$), cavity-induced single-atom interaction ($g_a$), and cavity-induced pair interaction ($g_\Delta$), as well as the pumping strength ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a mean-field description and operates in the far off-resonant dispersive regime, allowing for adiabatic elimination of excited states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup scheme, phase diagrams showing transitions between Normal, SF, CDW, and PDW phases based on interaction strength and pumping, and plots detailing the evolution of density and pairing harmonics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical setup and Hamiltonian to analyzing the system in different interaction regimes (repulsive vs. attractive) and finally detailing the joint instability leading to intertwined CDW+PDW states.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it explores how cavity-mediated light-matter interactions can engineer and stabilize exotic, multi-component ordered states (like intertwined CDW/PDW) in ultracold atomic systems, bridging quantum optics and many-body physics.

The cavity mode of frequency ωc is coupled to an internal atomic transition with coupling amplitude Ga(y) and to a molecular resonance with coupling strength G∆(y). The transverse plane wave pump laser of frequency ωP couples to both resonances, the single atom transition with strength Ωa(z) as well as the atom pair resonance with Ω∆(z). FIG. 2. Mean-field phase diagram and signatures of self-organization. (a) Zero temperature phase diagram as a function of the pump strength β (dimensionless) and the contact interaction strength g0/(ERλc) (dimensionless). The dashed horizontal lines mark cuts at g0/(ERλc) = ±0.101 shown in the following plots. The black dotted curve shows the analytical prediction. The labels denote the normal, superfluid (SF), charge-density-wave (CDW), pair-density-wave (PDW), and superradiant (SR) phases. The pale green region “weak pairing” corresponds to weak effective attraction, for which the exponentially small pairing amplitude is below our numerical accuracy.
